Full marks may be obtained for answers to ALL questions. Mathematical formulae booklets published by the GCE Board are allowed. In calculations, you are advised to show all the steps in your working, giving the answer at each stage. Calculators are allowed. Start each question on a fresh page.

questions.enonce_markdown: Given that $f(x) = \dfrac{x^2 + 18}{x(x^2 + 9)}$, express $f(x)$ in partial fractions. (3 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
The denominator has a linear factor $x$ and an irreducible quadratic factor $x^2 + 9$, so
$$\frac{x^2 + 18}{x(x^2 + 9)} \equiv \frac{A}{x} + \frac{Bx + C}{x^2 + 9}.$$
Multiply through by $x(x^2 + 9)$:
$$x^2 + 18 \equiv A(x^2 + 9) + (Bx + C)x.$$
- $x = 0$: $18 = 9A$, so $A = 2$.
- Coefficient of $x^2$: $1 = A + B$, so $B = -1$.
- Coefficient of $x$: $0 = C$, so $C = 0$.

$$\boxed{f(x) = \frac2x - \frac{x}{x^2 + 9}}$$
Check at $x = 3$: $f(3) = \frac{27}{3 \times 18} = \frac12$ and $\frac23 - \frac{3}{18} = \frac23 - \frac16 = \frac12$.

questions.enonce_markdown: Given that $f(x) = \dfrac{x^2 + 18}{x(x^2 + 9)}$, show, using partial fractions, that $\displaystyle\int_2^4 f(x)\,dx = \ln\!\left(\frac{4\sqrt{13}}{5}\right)$. (4 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
Using $f(x) = \dfrac2x - \dfrac{x}{x^2 + 9}$:
$$\int \frac2x\,dx = 2\ln x, \qquad \int \frac{x}{x^2 + 9}\,dx = \frac12\ln(x^2 + 9)$$
(the second by the substitution $u = x^2 + 9$, or because the numerator is half the derivative of the denominator). Hence
$$\int_2^4 f(x)\,dx = \left[\,2\ln x - \tfrac12\ln(x^2 + 9)\,\right]_2^4 = \Big(2\ln 4 - \tfrac12\ln 25\Big) - \Big(2\ln 2 - \tfrac12\ln 13\Big).$$
Simplify using $2\ln 4 = 4\ln 2$ and $\tfrac12\ln 25 = \ln 5$:
$$= 4\ln 2 - \ln 5 - 2\ln 2 + \tfrac12\ln 13 = 2\ln 2 - \ln 5 + \ln\sqrt{13} = \ln\frac{4\sqrt{13}}{5}.$$
$$\boxed{\int_2^4 f(x)\,dx = \ln\!\left(\frac{4\sqrt{13}}{5}\right)} \quad (\approx 1.0593)$$
